graphEvents.label: Which commands are safe to start without asking and where should the policy live
Doctor manifest is the only explicit mutation classification
Command metadata carries no safety class
Auto and confirm modes already encode run versus ask

label: The doctor route manifest is the only command set with an explicit mutation class: 16 read-only, 3 add-only and 22 mutates entries, each with a gate3_location naming what it writes.
The 19 command-metadata entries carry no mutation or safety field; their schema is command, ownerMode, description, argumentHint, userIntent, choreography and discriminator.

Every create command ships :auto (no approval prompts) and :confirm (pause at each step); deep-research uses approvals none versus multi_gate, and speckit-plan has both step_by_step and autonomous branches.

Gate 3 already implements ask-before-write at framework level, firing on file writes and excluding read-only review, audit, inspect and explain, but it acts after the workflow is chosen rather than at recommendation time.

The advisor's only safety mechanism is readOnlyRouteAllowed, which consults skill.readOnly; a mutating command that passes on a write-intent prompt is recommended with no ask marker and the brief has no field to carry one.

Recommended policy: carry a three-class safety map of read-only, add-only and mutating plus the write root in each command's metadata; run read-only immediately, run add-only when the target is explicit, and ask for mutating or unclear targets, with Gate 3 as the backstop.
Always asking for mutating commands would conflict with the shipped :auto mode, so the run-or-ask default must be overridable by a typed :auto or :confirm suffix and by explicit user instruction.

direction: Reusing readOnlyRouteAllowed as the whole policy
reason: It has no ask state and no write root, so it can suppress a recommendation but cannot tell the model what to do next
It contradicts the shipped :auto mode and adds a question before every read-only command
